english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for someone receiving hospitality at a private home or other place.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for someone visiting or staying with another person.

examples.english: I invited a guest to my home for dinner tonight.
examples.traditional: 我今晚請咗個客人嚟屋企食飯。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 maan5 ceng2 zo2 go3 haak3 jan4 lai4 uk1 kei2 sik6 faan6

examples.english: A visitor is coming to stay at my place for a few days.
examples.traditional: 有個客人嚟我屋企住幾日。
examples.jyutping: jau5 go3 haak3 jan4 lai4 ngo5 uk1 kei2 zyu6 gei2 jat6

english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a customer or someone using a service.
This is the all-purpose spoken choice for a customer of a shop, restaurant, or similar business.
Use this especially for a customer in a shop, restaurant, hotel, or other service setting, though it can also mean guest.
Use this colloquial term when the consumer is a customer dealing with a shop or service provider.

examples.english: This client wants to buy this phone.
examples.traditional: 呢位客人想買呢部手機。
examples.jyutping: nei1 wai2 haak3 jan4 soeng2 maai5 ni1 bou6 sau2 gei1

examples.english: Every patron at this cha chaan teng says the milk tea is good.
examples.traditional: 呢間茶記每個客人都話啲奶茶好飲。
examples.jyutping: ne1 gaan1 caa4 gei3 mui5 go3 haak3 jan4 dou1 waa6 di1 naai5 caa4 hou2 jam2

examples.english: The customer said they wanted another iced lemon tea.
examples.traditional: 客人話要加多杯凍檸茶。

examples.english: The consumer can ask the waiter to change tables.
